primary.title: Physics-Based Validation: The Foundation Of Trustworthy Agentic EDA
primary.snippet: This is the third article in a series examining what it takes to build production-ready AI agents for EDA. The first explored the architectural decisions required for agents to operate reliably in production environments. The second examined what self-verifying means in an agentic EDA workflow: how agents continuously check their decisions as they work, rather than waiting until the end of a run. But what exactly are those decisions being verified against? The answer is physics. More specifically, the deterministic, physics-based EDA engines that define whether a design is correct. A self-verifying agent checks its own work, and a physics-validated workflow confirms that work is correct. Semiconductor design is governed by physics Chip design has always faced physics-based constraints. Implemented in TSMC 65-nm CMOS at 335 MHz, the peripheral framework occupies 1769.760 {\mu}m2 post-synthesis and 1982.131 {\mu}m2 post-PnR. primary.title: Dual Strategy of Electroless Metal Deposition and Surface Silylation Toward Scalable Low-Temperature Hybrid Bonding for Advanced Packaging Applications
primary.snippet: The growing demand for high-performance computing and compact electronics has driven the transition toward advanced three-dimensional (3D) packaging technologies. Traditional packaging technologies, such as micro-bump interconnections, face limitations in achieving sub-micrometer pitches, prompting the development of alternative bonding strategies. Among them, Cu/SiO2 hybrid bonding (HB) has emerged as a promising method for enabling fine-pitch, high-density interconnects in next-generation semiconductor packaging. In this study, a reliable low-temperature Cu/SiO2 HB process was developed by combining metal electroless deposition (ELD) on sub-micron pitch Cu pads with selective surface functionalization of the SiO2 dielectric layer using silane. primary.title: Adapting DNNs to Embrace Voltage Scaling Induced Errors via Accumulation-Aware Quantization
primary.snippet: arXiv:2610.33824v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: The pervasive deployment of Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) across the computing spectrum has brought growing attention to energy efficiency, alongside raw performance. While voltage scaling is a potent knob for power reduction, its application in next-generation nodes is hampered by severe throughput degradation and susceptibility to process variation. This work aims to address these energy-reliability trade-offs by introducing a hardware-software co-design methodology, based on the observation that timing-robust bit ranges within the accumulator of a systolic array vary significantly across different voltage-frequency operating points. At the software level, we propose an Accumulation-Aware Training approach that incorporates this information as a first-order optimization constraint during training. primary.title: RFChipAgent: Multi-Agentic AI Flow for Analog/RF Chip Design
primary.snippet: Analog/RF circuits remain the critical interface between digital computation and the physical world, and emerging standards from Wi-Fi 7 to 6G place stringent demands on them, yet analog/RF design remains one of the most labor-intensive steps in chip development. We present RFChipAgent, a first-of-its-kind multi-agent flow of large language model (LLM) agents for end-to-end analog/RF circuit design automation, in which AI agents collaboratively orchestrate the complete design flow under human supervision. RFChipAgent is built around four technical pillars. First, a multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) subsystem with private per-document FAISS indexing extracts design knowledge from existing engineering documentation. science.title: Edge AI for Smart Cities: From Insight to Cognitive Action
science.snippet: This white paper explains how edge AI and physical AI help cities move beyond passive monitoring. It shows how urban infrastructure can sense, reason, and act on real-time conditions across public safety, mobility, and infrastructure management. What you will learn about: How the shift from smart cities to cognitive cities depends on infrastructure that reasons and acts, rather than infrastructure that only monitors. Why edge AI supports low-latency decisions, keeps sensitive data within city boundaries, and reduces dependency on centralized cloud infrastructure. How computer vision, multimodal sensing, and generative and agentic systems work together to support public safety, mobility, and infrastructure applications. science.title: Unification of Gravity and Standard Model: Weyl-Dirac-Born-Infeld action
science.snippet: arXiv:2508.10959v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We construct a unified (quantum) description, by the gauge principle, of gravity and Standard Model (SM), that generalises the Dirac-Born-Infeld action to the SM and Weyl geometry, hereafter called Weyl-Dirac-Born-Infeld action (WDBI). The theory is formulated in $d =4-2\epsilon$ dimensions. The WDBI action is a general gauge theory of SM and Weyl group (of dilatations and Poincar\'e symmetry), in the Weyl gauge covariant (metric!) formulation of Weyl geometry. The theory is SM and Weyl gauge invariant in $d=4-2\epsilon$ dimensions and there is no Weyl anomaly. The WDBI action has the unique elegant feature, not present in other gauge theories or even in string theory, that it is mathematically well-defined in $d=4-2\epsilon$ dimensions with no need to introduce in the action a UV regulator scale or field. science.title: Dark Matter Coherent Freeze-Out Mechanism: A Comprehensive Analysis
science.snippet: arXiv:2610.36049v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Both Weakly-Interacting Massive Particle (WIMP) and Axion-Like Particle (ALP) are attractive particle dark matter candidates. In this paper we consider a scenario in which both WIMP and ALP are present. The two species interact via a non-derivative quadratic coupling modeled on the axion-nucleon interaction in QCD. We show that even a small (Planck-suppressed) coupling can drastically modify the cosmological history of both species. In the very early Universe, the ALP field acquires a vacuum expectation value, and the system undergoes an inverse phase transition at a temperature around or below the weak scale. WIMPs may remain in equilibrium far beyond the usual freeze-out time, eventually decoupling via a novel "coherent freeze-out" mechanism. WIMP annihilation cross sections several orders of magnitude above the canonical thermal target

science.title: The Fate of 1/4-BPS States in the D1-D5 CFT
science.snippet: arXiv:2610.36057v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We consider the 1/4-BPS operators in the D1-D5 system on AdS$_3\times S^3\times T^4$. We evaluate the anomalous dimensions of low-lying sectors in conformal perturbation theory around Sym$^N(T^4)$ exactly in $N$. All anomalous dimensions are consistent with recombination of the short multiplets into long ones and take a particularly simple form. We show that at finite $N$ and at first nontrivial order in the deformation, for the sectors we consider, the BPS density of states agrees with that of the supergravity point. To the order in conformal perturbation theory we consider, this confirms that not all states that can get lifted do get lifted.

reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.37104v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distinguishing Purkinje cell (PC) simple spikes (SSs) from complex spikes (CSs) is key to studying cerebellar function. PC recordings commonly rely on wired headstages, whose tethers restrict natural movement in freely behaving animals. Untethered headstages remove this constraint, but cannot continuously transmit raw recordings within their power budgets, making on-headstage spike classification an attractive form of compression, provided it runs accurately in real time on constrained hardware. This work presents two compact spiking neural networks (SNNs) matched to their target hardware: ConvSNN, which maps to the Matrix Vector Processor (MVP) of an EFM32PG28 microcontroller, and StreamSNN, which processes one waveform value per timestep using learned time constants and fixed synaptic delays for a dedicated SKY130 circuit. reserve.title: Serotonin signaling enhances phagocytosis by brain macrophages through Htr2b and alleviates brain injury after stroke
reserve.snippet: Nature Neuroscience, Published online: 28 October 2026; doi:10.1038/s41593-026-02482-y The serotonin receptor Htr2b activation enhances lysosome biogenesis and phagocytic clearance of debris to mitigate neuroinflammation and brain injury after stroke. The study proposes a potential monocyte-derived macrophage-targeted immune therapy to improve neurological outcomes after ischemic stroke.

reserve.title: How Much Can Semiconductor Models Hide?
reserve.snippet: Key Takeaways: Advanced packaging pushes process behavior across company lines, so what one supplier hides now shapes another company’s prediction. Encryption and abstraction protect the recipe cleanly, but neither tells the receiving engineer where the model stops being valid. A model can be accurate and still be wrong for the question asked, making its envelope as much a deliverable as the model. The goal seems simple — share the model without sharing the process. A materials supplier shouldn’t have to reveal a proprietary formulation just so a customer can predict how it will behave in a package, and a foundry shouldn’t have to hand over its recipe to provide a useful model of a chiplet. But advanced packaging is making that separation much harder to maintain. reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36087v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Standard sirens provide a direct probe of the cosmic distance-redshift relation and therefore a powerful test of whether gravitational waves (GWs) propagate as predicted by general relativity on cosmological scales. In many extensions of general relativity, GW propagation is modified by an anomalous friction term, which alters the amplitude evolution and leads to a GW luminosity distance that differs from its electromagnetic counterpart. In this work, we develop a non-parametric reconstruction of this anomalous friction from dark standard sirens. reserve.title: Improved Gauge Conditions for Large Expansion Cosmological Models
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36123v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This study develops a new gauge condition for performing long duration numerical evolutions of Einstein's equation on cosmological spacetimes with non-trivial spatial topologies. This new gauge makes it possible to perform reliable numerical evolutions on these manifolds in which the spatial volumes become more than one million times larger. This new condition was tested for this study by evolving homogeneous and isotropic initial data on exemplar manifolds with three spatial topologies: Sixth-Turn space, the lens space L(5,2), and the Seifert fiber space SFS[S2:(2,1)(2,1)(2,-1)].

In effective field theory (EFT) extensions of GR, higher-curvature operators modify the binary dynamics and introduce corrections to the inspiral phase. reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36730v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: This paper investigates the greybody factor and Joule-Thomson expansion of deformed Schwarzschild-AdS black hole models. reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36863v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We study the possibility of the formation of primordial black holes (PBHs) using an inflaton potential constructed by stabilizing all K\"{a}hler moduli employing both the perturbative and non-perturbative corrections in the large volume scenario in type-IIB/F string theory. We further introduce a small perturbation in one of the K\"{a}hler moduli that modifies the existing potential in the field space. reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36923v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We formulate a description of self-gravitating Schr\"odinger--Poisson (SP) solitons in curved spacetime using a local inertial frame centered on the soliton. In the weak-field and non-relativistic regime, the effect of the background spacetime is incorporated into the SP equations through an effective tidal potential determined by the spacetime curvature. We apply this framework to a soliton moving along a circular equatorial geodesic around a Kerr black hole. The tidal field contains stationary and time-dependent quadrupolar components, which induce a deformation of the soliton and an associated mass quadrupole moment. We formulate the quadrupolar response in terms of the tidal deformability and the dimensionless Love number. reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.37331v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: In this work, we investigate the geodesic dynamics and tidal force effects in neutral and electrically charged regular spacetimes inspired by T-duality. reserve.title: Weighing dark matter particles with gravitational waves
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.37638v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: It is commonly assumed that the mass of dark matter particles cannot be determined from their gravitational effects when dark matter behaves as collisionless matter. Here we show that extreme-mass-ratio inspirals observable by millihertz gravitational-wave observatories such as the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA) could measure the mass of ultralight dark matter particles in sufficiently dense dark matter spikes. The separation of scales between the two black holes allows ultralight dark matter to form a collisionless density spike around the massive primary while retaining wave effects in its interaction with the stellar-mass companion. reserve.title: How particle physics stops ultra-relativistic bubbles and shapes their gravitational waves
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36160v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The gravitational-wave spectrum produced by ultra-relativistic bubbles in a first-order cosmological phase transition can be approximated in terms of their energy density as a function of bubble size. Bubble collisions and post-collision classical evolution negligibly change it. The dominant energy loss is particle scattering, often in the Landau--Pomeranchuk--Migdal regime. So the GW spectrum depends on the particle-physics coupling (interpolating between the `envelope' and `bulk flow' limits), on the interaction type (gauge, Yukawa, scalar quartic, ...), and on whether particle number is conserved. Finally, we consider broken global symmetries, which give a mixture of `elastic' and `inelastic' collisions.

reserve.title: All Dark Matter as Primordial Black Holes: a Gravitational-Wave Test
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36177v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We propose a novel test for the hypothesis that the dark matter of the Universe is composed entirely by asteroidal-mass primordial black holes. It relies on detecting the stochastic gravitational-wave background generated by the coalescence onto rapidly spinning supermassive astrophysical black holes of the light primordial black holes accumulated in spherically symmetric spikes. We discuss the scenarios in which the signal can be observed by the future space-based gravitational-wave observatories LISA and DECIGO.

Its uncertainty affects the mass and radius at which the innermost stable circular orbit reaches the stellar surface, a condition that defines the transition between disks whose inner edge is set by the surface and those truncated by orbital instability. We quantify how measurements of the electric dipole polarizability of neutron-rich nuclei reduce the uncertainty in this transition and in the orbital properties at the disk inner edge. reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.37617v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The high-mass black hole population inferred from ground-based observations can substantially affect the number of binaries detectable by the Laser Interferometer Space Antenna (LISA). reserve.title: Metric--affine gravity with dynamical chronology protection
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2604.08511v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: Modified theories of gravity often introduce geometric structure beyond general relativity to address unresolved problems in the gravitational sector without invoking ad hoc matter fields. Mimetic gravity, for example, generates an effective cosmological dark sector by isolating the conformal mode of the metric, while Ho\v{r}ava--Lifshitz gravity attains power-counting renormalizability by endowing spacetime with a preferred dynamical foliation. reserve.title: Minimum lifetime of a black hole
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2605.03922v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We derive bounds on the lifetime of an evaporating black hole. The minimum lifetime bound follows from energy conservation and purification, within the framework of `asymptotically semiclassical spacetimes'. We discuss the energy-cost of entanglement purification and find a lower bound on the purification time of the black hole, which scales as $M_0^4/\hbar^{3/2}$, where $M_0$ is the initial black hole mass. reserve.title: Heavy Black-Holes Also Matter in Standard Siren Cosmology
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2601.03257v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: With the release of the Gravitational-Wave Transient Catalog GWTC-4.0 by the LIGO-Virgo-KAGRA (LVK) collaboration, 218 candidate detections of gravitational waves (GWs) from compact binary coalescences (CBCs) have been reported. primary.title: Introducing Build-A-Chip-Bench: From Workload Specification to GDS
primary.snippet: Existing chip design benchmarks test isolated steps, such as writing RTL from a specification, and are increasingly saturated. ChipAgents is developing Build-A-Chip-Bench with contributions from Nvidia to the benchmark suite and scoring rubric. The benchmark evaluates AI agents from workload specification through GDS layout, using open-source tools and an open-source PDK to assess their ability to complete the chip-design workflow. Each design must pass a hard gate, covering functional correctness against a hidden verification IP as well as routability, hold timing, and DRC, and designs that pass are scored on PPA against the task’s constraints. The best agent passes the hard gate on 65% of tasks and reaches an overall score of 16.6%. primary.snippet: arXiv:2610.35935v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Video on SPI-attached microcontroller displays is limited less by decoding than by where each byte lives and which stages run serially. primary.title: Physics-Based Validation: The Foundation Of Trustworthy Agentic EDA
primary.snippet: This is the third article in a series examining what it takes to build production-ready AI agents for EDA. The first explored the architectural decisions required for agents to operate reliably in production environments. The second examined what self-verifying means in an agentic EDA workflow: how agents continuously check their decisions as they work, rather than waiting until the end of a run. But what exactly are those decisions being verified against? The answer is physics. More specifically, the deterministic, physics-based EDA engines that define whether a design is correct. A self-verifying agent checks its own work, and a physics-validated workflow confirms that work is correct. primary.title: SiMOS quantum-dot spin qubits enabled by extreme-ultraviolet lithography
primary.snippet: The realization of large-scale silicon quantum processors requires spin qubits compatible with advanced semiconductor manufacturing technologies, demanding lithographic processes that combine nanometer-scale precision with exceptional uniformity. Although the highest-performing silicon spin qubits demonstrated to date have relied on electron-beam (e-beam) lithography, its serial exposure process limits reproducibility studies and wafer-scale fabrication. science.snippet: Like many a nerd, I have a certain fascination with locks. This originates in reading the memoir Surely You’re Joking, Mr. Feynman as a teenager, in which Richard Feynman recounts picking locks and cracking combinations while at his day job working on the Manhattan Project at Los Alamos. science.snippet: arXiv:2610.37104v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Distinguishing Purkinje cell (PC) simple spikes (SSs) from complex spikes (CSs) is key to studying cerebellar function. PC recordings commonly rely on wired headstages, whose tethers restrict natural movement in freely behaving animals. Untethered headstages remove this constraint, but cannot continuously transmit raw recordings within their power budgets, making on-headstage spike classification an attractive form of compression, provided it runs accurately in real time on constrained hardware. reserve.title: How Much Can Semiconductor Models Hide?
reserve.snippet: Key Takeaways: Advanced packaging pushes process behavior across company lines, so what one supplier hides now shapes another company’s prediction. Encryption and abstraction protect the recipe cleanly, but neither tells the receiving engineer where the model stops being valid. A model can be accurate and still be wrong for the question asked, making its envelope as much a deliverable as the model. The goal seems simple — share the model without sharing the process. A materials supplier shouldn’t have to reveal a proprietary formulation just so a customer can predict how it will behave in a package, and a foundry shouldn’t have to hand over its recipe to provide a useful model of a chiplet. reserve.title: How particle physics stops ultra-relativistic bubbles and shapes their gravitational waves
reserve.snippet: arXiv:2610.36160v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: The gravitational-wave spectrum produced by ultra-relativistic bubbles in a first-order cosmological phase transition can be approximated in terms of their energy density as a function of bubble size. So the GW spectrum depends on the particle-physics coupling (interpolating between the `envelope' and `bulk flow' limits), on the interaction type (gauge, Yukawa, scalar quartic, ...), and on whether particle number is conserved. Finally, we consider broken global symmetries, which give a mixture of `elastic' and `inelastic' collisions.
